title: Finite Tor amplitude under the site comparison
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum, a prime $\ell\ne p$, an integer
$n\geq1$ and $A=A_{E,n}$, and let $T$ be a scheme on which $\ell$ is
invertible. Write $\nu_T:T_{\Proet}\to T_{\Et}$ for the comparison
morphism of sites.

1. **(i)** If $K'\in D^b_c(T_{\Et},A)$ has finite Tor amplitude in
$[a,b]$ on the étale site, in the sense of the étale clause of
[lem-sf-flat-model], then $\nu_T^*K'$ is bounded constructible on
$T_{\Proet}$ and has finite Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ in the sense of
[def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude].
1. **(ii)** Conversely, if $K\in D^b_c(T_{\Proet},A)$ has finite Tor
amplitude in $[a,b]$ and $K\cong\nu_T^*K'$ for a bounded-below complex
$K'$ of $A$-module sheaves on $T_{\Et}$, then $K'$ has finite Tor
amplitude in $[a,b]$ on the étale site.

proof.text: Clause (i): combine preserved bounded constructibility with the flat-model proof of preserved Tor amplitude. These are separate components, with no rephrasing of the conjunction as a new assumption.

For clause (ii), put A = A_{E,n}, which is finite for n >= 1. Regard K' as an object of D+ using the given bounded-below hypothesis. The ordered interval follows from HasProEtaleTorAmplitude. Apply the reverse implication of lem-exc-comparison-tor-interval. Its intrinsic realization after the bounded-below site pullback is canonically isomorphic to the derived functor of their composite, by mapDerivedCategoryCompIso. Compose this isomorphism with the given K isomorphism. Transport the pro-etale Tor predicate along it: any representative isomorphism Q(L) to the iterated pullback composes with its inverse to give Q(L) to K, and hence the original universal K-flat tensor test supplies the identical vanishing conclusion. This proves the premise of the reverse implication and therefore the etale Tor bound. No new constructibility or tensor-boundedness hypothesis is introduced. The composition isomorphism is the already proved source-library declaration CategoryTheory.Functor.mapDerivedCategoryCompIso; no derived-Kan-extension theorem is used.

source.place: Converse implication, specialized to the finite ring A_{E,n}; canonical derived composition and representative-isomorphism transport.

proof_origin.place: G7: retain the existing clause (i) proof; clause (ii) reuses the existing general finite-ring comparison Tor-interval equivalence with canonical derived-composition and isomorphism transport.
